# PinMeTo web presence rubric, v2.15.0-skill.1

<!-- Generated by scripts/render-rubric.mjs from references/rubric.md and the Theme mapping in references/artifact-report.md. Do not edit by hand: run `node scripts/render-rubric.mjs` after changing either. -->

This page explains how the PinMeTo web presence scan scores a multi-location brand. It is the same contract the scan runs (`references/rubric.md`), laid out for reading. The rubric is derived from PinMeTo's MLPR product rubric (MLPR 2.8.0); the differences are listed at the end.

## How the score is built

Every check returns a status: **pass**, **warn** or **fail**. Checks are weighted inside their pillar, pillars are weighted into the overall score, and the overall score maps to a grade.

| Pillar | Share of overall score | What it covers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SEO | 30% | The store locator and the per-location landing pages: can search engines crawl, understand and rank them? |
| GEO | 30% | The brand's real listings on Google, Apple and Bing Maps, read in a browser: do they exist, are they accurate, and do they agree with each other and with the page? |
| AIO | 25% | Whether generative answers (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity) can ground on the brand's own pages. |
| Agent Readiness | 15% | Whether AI agents acting for a customer can discover what the site offers and what they are allowed to do. |

| Grade | Overall score |
| --- | --- |
| A | 90 and above |
| B | 75 and above |
| C | 60 and above |
| D | 45 and above |
| F | below 45 |

| Status | Points earned | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| pass | 100% of the check's weight | Evaluated and passed. |
| warn | 50% | Could not be measured (no browser, blocked fetch, consent wall). An evidence gap, not a failure. |
| fail | 0% | Evaluated and failed. |

Two refinements. A **gradient** check earns its measured ratio instead of all or nothing (for example structured-data richness at 55 out of 100 earns 55% of its weight). A check that reads page markup and finds the value only after JavaScript runs earns **rendered-only credit** of 50%, because Google renders JavaScript but the crawlers that feed AI training and retrieval do not. Both sets of checks are marked in the tables below.

**Sampling.** Brands with fewer than 20 locations are scanned on 5 locations (or all of them, when there are fewer); larger brands on 10. The sample is pinned and reused on every re-run so scores stay comparable. A report needs at least 3 locations.

## SEO (30% of the overall score)

The store locator and the per-location landing pages: can search engines crawl, understand and rank them?

| Check | Weight in pillar | What it looks for | Passes when | Scoring notes | Theme |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `seo.localbusiness_jsonld_present` | 15 | Each location page carries LocalBusiness structured data (JSON-LD) in the HTML the server sends. | present on >=80% of sampled pages | gradient, rendered-only credit | Put each location's and your brand's details into the page code |
| `seo.localbusiness_jsonld_richness` | 10 | That structured data is complete: name, address, coordinates, URL and phone, plus hours, images, reviews and other optional fields. | gradient 0-100, see richness_rule | gradient, rendered-only credit | Put each location's and your brand's details into the page code |
| `seo.canonical_present` | 5 | Each location page names itself as the canonical URL, and that URL answers with 200. | present, resolves 200 | rendered-only credit | Let search engines find and crawl every location page |
| `seo.meta_title_unique` | 5 | No two sampled location pages share the same title. | no duplicates across sample | rendered-only credit | Make every location page introduce its own location |
| `seo.h1_unique_has_location` | 5 | Each page's main heading is unique and names the location. | >=80% of sample | gradient, rendered-only credit | Make every location page introduce its own location |
| `seo.hreflang_correct` | 5 | Multi-market sites link each page to its language versions, including itself, and the links are reciprocal. | self-ref + reciprocal (multi-market only) | rendered-only credit | Let search engines find and crawl every location page |
| `seo.sitemap_lists_locations` | 5 | The XML sitemap lists the location pages the crawl discovered. | >=80% of discovered locations | gradient | Let search engines find and crawl every location page |
| `seo.robots_allows_locations` | 5 | robots.txt does not block any sampled location page. | all sampled URLs accessible |  | Let search engines find and crawl every location page |
| `seo.og_twitter_per_location` | 5 | Each location page has its own Open Graph and Twitter preview tags. | >=80% present | gradient, rendered-only credit | Make every location page introduce its own location |
| `seo.lcp_sample` | 10 | The main content of a location page appears within 2.5 seconds on a phone, measured by PageSpeed Insights on three sampled pages. | lab LCP <2.5s on >=80% of 3 sampled URLs | gradient | Make location pages fast on phones |
| `seo.mobile_friendly` | 5 | Each sampled page declares a mobile viewport in its served HTML. | configured viewport on all sampled pages | rendered-only credit | Make location pages fast on phones |
| `seo.image_alt_text` | 5 | Images on the location pages carry alt text. | >=90% present | gradient, rendered-only credit | Make every location page introduce its own location |
| `seo.meta_description_unique` | 5 | No two sampled location pages share the same meta description. | no duplicates | rendered-only credit | Make every location page introduce its own location |
| `seo.internal_linking_depth` | 10 | Every location page is reachable within three clicks of the homepage. | all within 3 clicks of homepage | gradient, rendered-only credit | Let search engines find and crawl every location page |
| `seo.breadcrumbs_structured` | 5 | Location pages show a breadcrumb trail and describe it with BreadcrumbList structured data. | BreadcrumbList schema + visible breadcrumb | rendered-only credit | Let search engines find and crawl every location page |

### How `seo.localbusiness_jsonld_richness` is scored

JSON-LD parses with no schema errors (else score = 0). Then:

| Properties | Points out of 100 |
| --- | --- |
| Required together: name, address, geo, url, telephone | 40 |
| `openingHoursSpecification` | 10 |
| `image[logo+cover]` | 10 |
| `areaServed` | 5 |
| `paymentAccepted` | 5 |
| `amenityFeature` | 5 |
| `hasOfferCatalog\|makesOffer` | 5 |
| `review\|aggregateRating` | 10 |
| `sameAs` | 5 |
| `contactPoint` | 5 |

## GEO (30% of the overall score)

The brand's real listings on Google, Apple and Bing Maps, read in a browser: do they exist, are they accurate, and do they agree with each other and with the page?

GEO is scored in three sub-groups:

| Sub-group | Share of GEO | What it measures |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A. Per platform | 55% | Share of applicable checks passed on each platform, weighted Google 55 / Apple 30 / Bing 15. |
| B. Cross-platform consistency | 25% | Whether the platforms agree with each other, with the PinMeTo record as the reference. |
| C. Platform-to-page agreement | 20% | Whether the location page agrees with the platforms' dominant answer (majority vote across Google + Apple + Bing after normalization; Google wins ties). |

### A. Per-platform checks

| Check | Platforms | What it looks for | Theme |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `geo.listing_connected_pinmeto` | Google, Apple, Bing | The location's listing on this platform is connected and managed through PinMeTo, and the listing on the map does not contradict the PinMeTo record. | Connect every listing through PinMeTo |
| `geo.name_matches_site` | Google, Apple, Bing | The listing's name matches the location page, ignoring case, punctuation and legal suffixes. | Same name, address, phone and pin everywhere |
| `geo.address_matches_site` | Google, Apple, Bing | The listing's address matches the location page after postal normalization. | Same name, address, phone and pin everywhere |
| `geo.phone_matches_site` | Google, Apple, Bing | The listing's phone number matches the location page in international format. | Same name, address, phone and pin everywhere |
| `geo.website_url_on_listing` | Google, Bing | The listing links to the right location page, not just the homepage. | Same name, address, phone and pin everywhere |
| `geo.coords_within_50m` | Google, Apple, Bing | The map pin sits within 50 metres of the location's recorded coordinates. | Same name, address, phone and pin everywhere |
| `geo.location_platform_parity` | Google, Apple, Bing | Brand-wide: every location has a listing on each platform, with no duplicates and no stale permanently-closed pages. | Connect every listing through PinMeTo |
| `geo.hours_present` | Google | The Google listing shows opening hours. | Keep each Google listing complete and fresh |
| `geo.special_hours_set` | Google | Holiday hours are set, read from Google near a holiday and otherwise from the PinMeTo record. | Keep each Google listing complete and fresh |
| `geo.photos_5_plus` | Google | The Google listing has at least five photos. | Keep each Google listing complete and fresh |
| `geo.services_attributes` | Google | The Google listing lists services or attributes. | Keep each Google listing complete and fresh |
| `geo.menu_order_reservations` | Google | For restaurants, cafes, hotels, salons and clinics: the Google listing offers a menu, ordering or reservations link. | Keep each Google listing complete and fresh |
| `geo.recent_reviews_180d` | Google | The Google listing has a review from the last 180 days. | Keep each Google listing complete and fresh |
| `geo.consumer_alerts_clear` | Google | The Google listing shows no consumer alert. | Keep each Google listing complete and fresh |

Each platform's score is the share of its applicable checks that passed. A listing that was searched for and not found scores zero on that platform. A listing nobody could look at (no browser, consent wall) scores as **warn** on every check instead, because the scan must not report a missing listing on evidence it does not have.

### B. Cross-platform consistency

| Field | Weight in sub-group | What it looks for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `consistency.name` | 35 | The location's name agrees across Google, Apple and Bing, with the PinMeTo record as the reference. |
| `consistency.address` | 35 | The location's address agrees across the three platforms, with the PinMeTo record as the reference. |
| `consistency.coords_50m_cluster` | 30 | The three platforms' pins sit within 50 metres of each other and of the PinMeTo coordinates. |

Scored against the PinMeTo record as the reference value: 100 if every observed platform matches it after normalization, 50 if exactly one platform deviates, 0 if two or more deviate. Using the record as reference removes the two-platform tie (whichever listing deviates from PinMeTo is the deviant).

### C. Platform-to-page agreement

| Field | Weight in sub-group | What it looks for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `page.jsonld_name_matches_dominant` | 20 | The name in the location page's structured data matches the name the map platforms agree on. |
| `page.jsonld_telephone_matches_dominant` | 20 | The phone in the page's structured data matches the platforms' phone. |
| `page.jsonld_geo_within_50m_dominant` | 20 | The coordinates in the page's structured data sit within 50 metres of the platforms' pin. |
| `page.opening_hours_matches_dominant` | 20 | The page's opening hours match the platforms' hours. |
| `page.visible_nap_matches_dominant` | 20 | The name, address and phone a visitor reads on the page match the platforms. |

## Themes

The report groups failing checks into Themes: one plain-language issue that one fix and one owner resolve. Every point-bearing check belongs to exactly one Theme.

| Theme | Effort | What it covers | Checks |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Put each location's and your brand's details into the page code | One template change | Structured data (JSON-LD) that names each location and the brand in the HTML the server sends, so search engines and AI crawlers read it without running JavaScript. | 7 |
| Make every location page introduce its own location | One template change | Every location page carries its own title, description, heading, image text and social preview, so search engines can tell the pages apart and show the right one. | 5 |
| Let search engines find and crawl every location page | One developer task | Canonicals, sitemaps, robots rules, breadcrumbs, language links and link depth that let crawlers discover and index every location page. | 9 |
| Make location pages fast on phones | Performance work | Location pages show their main content within 2.5 seconds on mobile and pass Google's mobile-friendly test. | 2 |
| Give AI assistants a text version of your site | One developer task | A plain-text guide at /llms.txt and Markdown versions of pages on request, so AI assistants read your own words instead of third-party summaries. | 4 |
| Answer customers' questions on the page itself | Content task | Question-and-answer content, quick answers, speakable sections and author signals that AI search can quote directly. | 5 |
| Tell AI agents what they may do and give them a front door | A few small files | Content signals in robots.txt plus the well-known files (MCP server card, agent skills, API catalog, link headers) that tell AI agents what they may do and where to start. | 6 |
| Connect every listing through PinMeTo | PinMeTo task, no code | Every location's Google, Apple and Bing listing exists and is connected through PinMeTo, with no duplicates or stale closed pages. | 2 |
| Same name, address, phone and pin everywhere | Fix the record in PinMeTo, then the page | Name, address, phone, website, hours and map pin agree across the PinMeTo record, every map platform and the location page. | 13 |
| Keep each Google listing complete and fresh | Ongoing, no code | Each Google listing shows hours, holiday hours, five or more photos, services, recent reviews and no consumer alerts. | 7 |

## How this differs from the PinMeTo product rubric

The scan is a skill-line fork of MLPR MLPR 2.8.0. SEO, AIO and Agent Readiness are scored identically to the product. GEO differs in two ways, so GEO scores are not directly comparable with product scores:

- **Bing is a scored platform again.** The product dropped it because the Bing Maps Enterprise API is being retired; the skill reads the live bing.com/maps surface in a browser instead.
- **`geo.listing_connected_pinmeto` is new.** It measures whether each listing is connected and managed through PinMeTo, judged from the location record and downgraded when the map surface contradicts it.

A re-run always scores with the current rubric version. Earlier scans keep the scores they were computed with, and the report attributes every moved check to a rubric change, a measurement correction, or a real change on the site or listing. The version history is in `references/rubric.md`.
